Remark 9.2. We point out that one can also define analogues of these operators in the quasi-parabolic descendent algebras $\mathbb{D}_{\alpha \bullet}^{\text{qpar}}$; recall that this is a supercommutative algebras generated by symbols $\text{ch}_k(\gamma)$ for $\gamma \in H^*(C)$ and $\text{ch}_k(e_j)$ for $0 \leqslant j \leqslant l + 1$, modulo certain simple relations; alternatively, it is generated by $\text{ch}_k^H(\gamma), \text{ch}_k^H(e_j)$. One defines $\mathsf{L}_n^{\text{qpar}}: \mathbb{D}_{\alpha \bullet}^{\text{qpar}} \to \mathbb{D}_{\alpha \bullet}^{\text{qpar}}$ by $\mathsf{L}_n^{\text{qpar}} = \mathsf{R}_n^{\text{qpar}} + \mathsf{T}_n^{\text{qpar}}$ where $\mathsf{R}_n^{\text{qpar}}$ is defined exactly in the same way as in the parabolic case, and $\mathsf{T}_n$ is

$$\mathsf{T}_n^{\text{qpar}} = \sum_{a+b=n} a!b! \left( (1-g)\text{ch}_a(\text{pt})\text{ch}_b(\text{pt}) + \sum_{j=0}^l \text{ch}_a(e_j)\text{ch}_b(e_{j+1} - e_j) \right).$$

In particular, the Virasoro constraints do not depend on a choice of weights within a fixed chamber.

The main result of this section are the Virasoro constraints for moduli spaces of parabolic bundles:

**Theorem 9.3.** Let $\alpha = (r, d, f_\bullet, c) \in C(I)$. For every $D \in \mathbb{D}^{\text{par}}$ we have

$$\int_{[M_\alpha]} \mathsf{L}_{\text{wt}_0}(D) = 0.$$

These generalize the Virasoro constraints for moduli spaces of stable bundles shown in [BLM]. For the proof, we will need compatibility statements between the Virasoro constraints and the structures that we have discussed earlier in the paper: wall-crossing, flag bundles, and Hecke operators. We develop these compatibilities first, and then give the proof in Section 9.5.

9.1. Primary states and wall-crossing compatibility. Compatibility with wall-crossing is already the key ingredient in [BLM]. To state it, let us introduce the Lie subalgebra of primary states.

**Definition 9.4.** The space of primary states of weight $i$ on $\mathbf{V}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}}$ is

$$P_i = \{ v \in \mathbf{V}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}} : L_0(v) = iv \text{ and } L_n(v) = 0 \text{ for } n > 0 \}.$$

The space of primary states on the Lie algebra $\widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}}$ is

$$\breve{P}_0 = P_1 / T(P_0) \subseteq \widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}}.$$

By [LM, Corollary 5.7], a class $u \in \widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}}$ (of non-trivial topological type) is a primary state if and only if $L_{\text{wt}_0}(u) = 0$, where

$$L_{\text{wt}_0} = \sum_{n \geqslant -1} \frac{(-1)^n}{(n+1)!} L_{-1}^{n+1} \circ L_n: \widetilde{\mathbf{V}}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}} \to \mathbf{V}_{\text{tr}}^{\text{par}}$$

is the dual of $\mathsf{L}_{\text{wt}_0}$. In particular, the moduli space $M_\alpha$ satisfies the Virasoro constraints (i.e. Theorem 9.3 holds) if and only if $[M_\alpha] \in \breve{P}_0$ is a primary state.
